name: Cathedral, Alcázar and Archivo de Indias in Seville
description: In the heart of Seville, three neighbouring monuments tell the story of Andalusia. The vast Gothic cathedral, the largest of its style, holds Christopher Columbus's tomb and is crowned by the Giralda, a 12th-century Almohad minaret turned bell tower. Beside it stand the Moorish-flavoured Alcázar palace and the Archivo de Indias, which preserves records of Spain's American colonies.
